title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: exclude specific domains from web grounding
summary: Hold for a control-reference correction: the Cloud Policy link documents the policy-creation wizard but does not name the final web-search setting printed in the path. Microsoft documents that setting on the separately cited web-search page; the domain-exclusion script, limits and opt-in default are supported.

Administrators can exclude specified sites from web grounding in Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: By using domain exclusion, you can specify up to 1,000 sites to exclude from web grounding in Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Chat through a PowerShell script.

claims.claim: The exclusion limit is 1,000 sites or CSV entries.
claims.quote: Maximum of 1,000 entries per CSV file.

claims.quote: Currently, domain exclusions support filtering on web page results only.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Other answer verticals, such as news, might still cite an excluded site.
claims.quote: Results from other answer verticals, such as news, might still be cited.

claims.claim: Domain exclusion supports up to two levels of subdomains.
claims.quote: Currently, the domain exclusion configuration supports up to two levels of subdomains.

claims.claim: Tenant domain exclusions are managed with ConfigureTenantDomainExclusions.ps1, downloadable at aka.ms/Copilot/DomainExclusionScript.
claims.quote: To manage the Copilot domain exclusion configuration for your tenant, use the ConfigureTenantDomainExclusions.ps1 PowerShell script. Download it at https://aka.ms/Copilot/DomainExclusionScript.

claims.claim: The script can get the current domain exclusion configuration and export it to CSV.
claims.quote: Get the current domain exclusion configuration and export to CSV

claims.claim: ConfigureTenantDomainExclusions.ps1 -Create -FromFile <csv> creates a tenant exclusion configuration from CSV.
claims.quote:
Create your domain exclusion configuration from a CSV file:
   .\ConfigureTenantDomainExclusions.ps1 -Create -FromFile "input.csv"

claims.claim: The script supports updating an existing exclusion configuration from CSV.
claims.quote: Update an existing domain exclusion configuration from CSV file

claims.claim: The script supports deleting the current exclusion configuration.
claims.quote: Delete the current domain exclusion configuration

claims.claim: The script supports generating a template CSV.
claims.quote: Generate a template CSV file for domain exclusions

claims.claim: Domain exclusion is admin-opt-in: default settings contain no exclusion configuration, and an administrator opts in by running the script.
claims.quote: Default settings don't include the domain exclusion configuration. Opt in to use the feature by running the PowerShell script.

claims.claim: Cowork uses the organization's domain exclusion policy.
claims.quote: Cowork uses your organization's domain exclusion policies, including exclusions for specific domains.

claims.claim: The script is run as Search Administrator or Global Administrator.
claims.quote: Sign in as a Search Administrator or Global Administrator.

claims.claim: The script needs the Az.Accounts PowerShell module.
claims.quote: Az.Accounts PowerShell module (the ConfigureTenantDomainExclusions.ps1 script installs the module automatically if it's missing).

claims.claim: When web search is enabled, Copilot and Copilot Chat can fetch Bing web information to ground responses.
claims.quote: When web search is enabled, Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat may fetch information from the Bing search service when information from the web helps to provide a better, more grounded response.

claims.claim: Generated Bing search queries consist of a few words informed by the user's prompt.
claims.quote: This generated search query is different from the user's original prompt-it consists of a few words informed by the user's prompt.

claims.claim: Generated search queries do not include entire Microsoft 365 files.
claims.quote:
The following information isn't included in the generated search query sent to the Bing search service:
Entire Microsoft 365 files (for example, emails or documents) or files uploaded into Copilot

claims.claim: Generated search queries can be informed by organizational document content.
claims.quote: However, it may also be informed by data within a Microsoft 365 document under the following conditions:

claims.claim: A generated web query can use a manager's name retrieved from Microsoft 365 data.
claims.quote: Copilot finds the name of the user's manager from Microsoft 365 data. It then generates a Bing search query based on their name to see what information about them is available on the web.

claims.claim: A very short prompt can itself form the search query.
claims.quote: The user's entire prompt, unless the prompt is very short (for example, "local weather")

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Domain exclusion filters incoming grounding results rather than preventing generated search queries from being sent to Bing.
claims.quote: Currently, domain exclusions support filtering on web page results only. Results from other answer verticals, such as news, might still be cited.

claims.claim: Microsoft includes domain exclusion among its proactive prompt-defense protections.
claims.quote: Proactive protections reduce risk by improving visibility, limiting exposure to harmful content, controlling content discovery, and protecting customer data.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented domain-exclusion user messaging as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "domain exclusion" "user" "message" Copilot; Copilot domain exclusion user notification message wildcard top level domains. Opened Domain exclusion overview and prompt defense in depth; no feature-specific user message documented.

claims.claim: Wildcard-style blocking of whole top-level domains is not described for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot domain exclusion user notification message wildcard top level domains. Read Domain exclusion overview including CSV requirements and limitations; no whole-TLD wildcard syntax documented.

claims.claim: Government tenants have web search off by default.
claims.quote: By default, web search is enabled for Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat in commercial tenants, but not for U.S. Government Community Cloud (GCC, GCC-High, and DoD) tenants.

claims.claim: Declarative agents can scope web search to specific sites in their manifest.
claims.quote: To scope your web search to specific sites, add the sites property and specify up to four URLs, as shown in the following example.

claims.claim: The interaction between tenant exclusions and declarative-agent web search scoped to an excluded site is not documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: declarative agents scoped web search tenant domain exclusions excluded sites. Opened Domain exclusion overview and Add knowledge sources to your declarative agent; neither explains this interaction.

claims.claim: An admin UI for domain-exclusion configuration is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot domain exclusion admin center UI configuration. Opened Domain exclusion overview and Configure Microsoft Copilot settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center; only script-based domain exclusion management found.

claims.claim: The linked Cloud Policy overview documents the full path ending Configure Settings > Allow web search in Copilot.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph beta Cloud Policy Allow web search in Copilot PowerShell API policy configuration. Read overview-cloud-policy: wizard ends at selecting policies by name; Allow web search in Copilot appears on manage-public-web-access, not this row's docs page.
claims.fix: In controls[1].ui and its rendered table cell, shorten the path to 'Customization > Policy Management > Policy configurations > Create > Start with the basics > Choose the scope > Configure Settings'. Keep the existing docs URL. Keep the specific policy name in the surrounding prose, supported by https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/manage-public-web-access.

claims.claim: An automation equivalent for the Cloud Policy Allow web search in Copilot setting is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph beta Cloud Policy Allow web search in Copilot PowerShell API policy configuration; "Cloud Policy" "Graph" "configuration" API Microsoft 365 Apps. Read Cloud Policy overview and web-search controls; no setting-management call found.

claims.claim: Allow web search in Copilot is a Cloud Policy setting with enabled, disabled and disabled-in-work-mode-only options.
claims.quote:
Enabled in Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat
Disabled in Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat
Disabled in Microsoft Copilot Work mode; Enabled in Microsoft Copilot Web mode and Microsoft Copilot Chat

claims.claim: The web-search policy can target tenant-wide users or specific groups.
claims.quote: On the Choose the scope page, determine whether the policy configuration applies to all users, specific groups, or to users who anonymously access documents using Office for the web.

claims.claim: Users retain a personal web-search toggle when policy allows web search, but cannot enable it when policy disables web search.
claims.quote: If the IT admin turns off web search, the Web content toggle is turned off and appears dimmed. Users can't turn on the toggle to use web search.

claims.claim: The Purview path is Data Loss Prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Custom > Custom policy > Locations > Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork.
claims.quote:
Go to Data Loss Prevention > Policies and select + Create policy.
Select the Custom template, then Custom policy.
On the Locations page, set the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork location to on.

claims.claim: New-DlpCompliancePolicy -Name <name> -Locations <location> -EnforcementPlanes @('CopilotExperiences') creates the Copilot DLP policy container.
claims.quote: New-DLPCompliancePolicy -Name "Copilot Policy" -Locations $loc -EnforcementPlanes @("CopilotExperiences")

claims.claim: The web-search DLP rule uses Content contains > Sensitive information types.
claims.quote: Add a rule with the Content contains > Sensitive information types condition and choose the SITs you want to detect.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; controls[2].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Prevent Copilot from processing content > Performing Web Searches blocks external web search when the prompt contains configured sensitive information types.
claims.quote:
In the same rule, set the action to Prevent Copilot from processing content > Performing Web Searches.
Save and turn on the policy.
When a user prompt contains the configured SITs, Copilot and Cowork block external web search as a grounding source

claims.claim: The policy-creation cmdlet supports tenant scope but does not itself create the required DLP rule.
claims.quote:
For the entire tenant, use this value: {Type:"Tenant",Identity:"All"}.
The last command creates the DLP rule with the name "Copilot Rule" (use any unique name).

claims.claim: Copilot > Settings > Data access in the Microsoft 365 admin center links administrators to the web-search Cloud Policy configuration.
claims.quote: Follow the link from Copilot settings to create an Allow web search in Copilot cloud policy in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center.
